allometry.note: Rough stem heights from general knowledge: a few metres by 70 years, about 5 m by 120. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: dark green stems with 12 to 19 ribs, areoles 2 cm apart with dark felt, short dark radial spines and one to three longer centrals that grey with age; creamy white to lavender flowers. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): its tepals on a spiral (their count by hand: no flora counts them) on a floral cup above the inferior ovary, and a style with 5 to 15 stigma lobes, from the characters of Cactaceae and Stenocereus by the rules at the flowering plants. Its 200 stamens by hand, the most a flower draws, for the numerous ones every flora gives.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a clump of a dozen or more ribbed columns, 15 to 20 cm thick, that rise from a short base, spread out and curve up into a vase 3 to 7 m tall; new stems come from the base over decades. Pale flowers open near the stem tips, followed by red, spiny fruit. Not fitted to measurements.

generator.params.dioecious.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): a plant bears both sexes, unless its taxa state it dioecious.

generator.params.height_max.note: What the conifer and succulent programs' height_max means: the height their Chapman-Richards curve rises toward with age and never reaches, so the tallest the plant grows, the height a flora gives as its greatest ("trees to 40 m"). Plants of a usual age stand below it, as the curve says. Where a flora's greatest is a rare record, the plant grows a little tall; a check of the grown plant against its usual height (spec rework M8) will show it.

generator.params.radius_max.note: Spec rework E6c: a column's or barrel's girth from its stated diameter.

generator.params.sex.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): a plant's sex is its own draw, dealt across a package's seeds so that both sexes grow; the typical plant (sex 0.5) is female, so it shows its fruit.

generator.program.note: The cacti's own program (growth plan G2.3a): columns, barrels and chains of joints, their ribs, areoles and spines from each species' look.

generator.spreads.params.height_max.note: What the conifer and succulent programs' height_max means: the height their Chapman-Richards curve rises toward with age and never reaches, so the tallest the plant grows, the height a flora gives as its greatest ("trees to 40 m"). growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy (milestone F1). Calibration against measurements and photographs comes later.
